transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I guess things have just been getting on top of me. Since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve been snapping at my wife over stupid little house stuff, and I’m putting off jobs and paperwork I used to handle. Even when I’m in the workshop or out fishing, I can’t really get my head quiet.
Have you found that activities you used to enjoy, like working in the workshop or fishing, aren’t as pleasurable or interesting to you lately?
I don’t know… I still do them. I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped liking them exactly. It’s just harder to settle into it, I guess.
How long have you been feeling this way and noticing these changes in yourself?
About five months, I think. It started not long after my father-in-law moved in with us.
Have you been feeling down on yourself or blaming yourself for things more than usual?
I’m not sure. I mean… I get annoyed with myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m blaming myself all the time or anything.
Have you been feeling more tired or like you don’t have much energy, even when you’re not doing anything physically demanding?
I don’t know… maybe a little, but I haven’t really been keeping track. I wouldn’t say I’m exhausted all the time or anything.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or focusing on tasks, even ones you used to handle easily?

Yeah… some. I’ve been putting off paperwork and little jobs I used to just handle. I’ll go out to the workshop or try to fish, thinking I’ll clear my head, but it just keeps running. It’s hard to settle on one thing.
Have you felt less interested or less motivated to do things you usually enjoy, like working in the workshop or going fishing?

Yeah… I guess so. I still go out to the workshop or try to fish, but it doesn’t really feel the same. My head just keeps going, mostly since my father-in-law moved in, and I end up putting things off instead of just doing them.
Would you say you’re feeling down or sad most of the time now, even when you’re not thinking about your father-in-law or the house stuff?
I don’t think it’s most of the time, no. I mean… I get low sometimes, but it’s hard to separate it from all that stuff. If I’m not thinking about it, I’m not sure I’d call it sad exactly.
Would you say you’re feeling down or low in mood most days, even when you’re not thinking about the stress with your father-in-law or household issues?
No… I don’t think it’s most days like that. I mean, I have moments where I feel pretty low, but if I’m not thinking about all that, it’s not always there.
Would you say you have days where you feel low or down even when there’s nothing specific bothering you or when things are going smoothly?
I’m not sure. Maybe here and there, but I usually can point to something. If things are actually going okay, I don’t really notice feeling down for no reason.
Would you say that activities you used to enjoy, like working in the workshop or going fishing, feel less enjoyable or rewarding to you now compared to before?

Yeah… somewhat. I still go out to the workshop or try to fish, but my head doesn’t really quiet down like it used to. I end up thinking about the house stuff and everything with my father-in-law, so it’s… not as rewarding, I guess.
Would you say you feel down or low most days, even when you’re not thinking about the stress with your father-in-law or other household issues?
I don’t think so… I mean, I’ve said it’s hard to separate, but if I’m not thinking about all that, I don’t usually feel low most days. It’s more tied to what’s going on.
